chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
The divorce of a female slave is [equivalent to] her sale, or the sale of her husband.
And he said regarding a man who marries his female slave to another man and then sells her: 'It is the separation between them, unless the buyer wishes to keep them together.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for divorcing a female slave in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of *Faskh* (automatic dissolution) in the marriage of a female slave (*Ummah*), establishing that her sale or her husband's sale severs the marital bond due to the change in ownership. It highlights the practical flexibility granted to the new owner (*al-Mushtari*), who may choose to retain the couple together or enforce separation, reflecting the distinct legal status of slaves compared to free women in Shia jurisprudence. The narration underscores the principle that the master's right of disposal (*Tamlik*) directly impacts the continuity of the marital contract.
